To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an energy-efficient 3 tap decision feedback equalizer for high-speed communication systems.
we have proposed a closed-loop DFE architecture that utilizes a novel merged-latch-and-summer design for 1st-tap and merged-feedback-MUX-and-diff-pair for 2nd and the 3rd-tap stages.
a closed-loop architecture using three techniques to enable energy-efficient 3-Tap DFE to operate at 10-40Gb/s in a 65nm CMOC technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a 3-tap 40Gb/s DFE with a power efficiency of 0.67pJ/bit, a latency of 1.25ns, and a latency variation of 0.25ns, which is suitable for high-speed optical communication systems.
the design and implementation of energy-efficient 3-stage DFE for 40Gb/s optical interconnects.
a novel closed-loop architecture for 3-tap 40Gb/s DFE in 65nm technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed design techniques enable energy-efficient 3 tap DFE to operate at 10Gbaud in 65nm technology.
we have demonstrated a 40Gb/s energy-efficient 3-Tap DFE in 65nm technology, which achieves the lowest reported energy efficiency of 0.67pJ/bit.
the proposed 3-tap equalizer achieves 1.2ps rms jitter and 2.2dB equalization gain at 40Gb/S, with 27mW power consumption.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed closed-loop DFE is the first to operate at 3-tap and 40Gb/s, and the 1st and 2nd tap stages are the first to operate with 1.3pF load at 3-taps and 40Gb/S, respectively.
we successfully design the 3-taps DFE in a 40Gb/s system, and the power consumption is 27mWs.
the proposed closed-loop 3-tap architecture is able to provide a power-efficient solution for high-speed equalizer design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed 3-tap equalizer is capable of operating at 40Gb/lane with 27mW power consumption, and the energy efficiency can be further reduced by 2X with 3-tap architecture.

a DFE with a closed-loop architecture can operate at a 40Gb/s data rate with a power efficiency that is comparable to a conventional open-loop DFE, and that it can be designed with a similar complexity as a conventional open-loop design.
the proposed techniques can be applied to any tap stages in the 3-taps DFE design, and thus can be easily extended to higher speed and/or lower power consumption applications.
